national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of children in Bosnia and Herzegovina between the age of three and the starting age of compulsory primary education who attend preschool education programmes. These programmes include organised educational, care and protection activities that support children’s cognitive, physical and socio-emotional development.
national_rationale: The data source is preschool education statistics published by the Agency for Statistics of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BHAS). Data are collected through annual statistical reports from preschool institutions and preschool education programmes, including preparatory programmes for children before starting school. BHAS consolidates and publishes data collected by the competent statistical institutions and the Brčko District of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The share is determined by comparing the number of children of the relevant age enrolled in preschool education with the total population of the same age group. Progress is assessed based on changes in the indicator value over time. An increase in the share of children participating in early childhood education and care programmes indicates positive progress towards this objective. The progress shown reflects the trend in the indicator over the observed period and does not represent the degree of achievement of a specific national target.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers children between the age of three and the starting age of compulsory primary education who attend preschool programmes. The data are based on the statistical coverage of children enrolled in preschool institutions and preparatory programmes before starting school. Comparisons with EU data should take into account differences in the organisation of preschool education, age groups and programme classification, particularly with regard to the alignment of national programmes with ISCED level 0.
national_long_objective: Increasing the availability of and participation in preschool education is an important direction for the development of the education system in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Reform Agenda of Bosnia and Herzegovina envisages that, by June 2027, enrolment in preschool education should reach 50% among children aged 3 to 5, while a target of 60% is set for children in the year before starting school. A target enrolment rate of 15% is envisaged for children aged 0 to 2. These targets refer to different age groups and represent reform targets for 2027, rather than a single target value for the overall coverage of this indicator.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of children between the age of three and the starting age of compulsory primary education who participate in early childhood education and care (ECEC) programmes that can be classified as ISCED level 0 according to the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED 2011). To be classified as ISCED level 0, ECEC programmes must be intentionally designed to support a child’s cognitive, physical and socio-emotional development. The starting age of compulsory primary education varies across countries. Programmes that are not intentionally designed to support child development, such as childcare-only programmes, are not included in this indicator.
eu_rationale: The data source is the European Statistical System (ESS). Enrolment data for early childhood education and care programmes are collected through the joint UNESCO-OECD-Eurostat (UOE) data collection on education statistics, while population data are obtained from Eurostat population statistics. The indicator is calculated as the share of children participating in the relevant programmes in the total population of the corresponding age group. Data are disseminated annually, with the school year as the reference period.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers children between the age of three and the starting age of compulsory primary education who participate in early childhood education and care programmes classified at ISCED level 0. The starting age of compulsory primary education varies across countries and is taken into account when determining the coverage. Data are comparable across countries reporting in accordance with the common UOE methodological framework. The time series is available from 2013 onwards.
eu_long_objective: Participation in early childhood education and care is an important precondition for children’s development, the acquisition of basic knowledge and skills, the reduction of inequalities and successful progression to later stages of education. Under the Strategic Framework for European Cooperation in Education and Training for the period 2026–2030, the target is for at least 96% of children between the age of three and the starting age of compulsory primary education to participate in early childhood education and care by 2030. This target represents a collective EU reference level and is not an individual target for each Member State.
